name: ETB / Flicker
summary: Enter-the-battlefield trigger loops backed by flicker (exile-and-return) effects, end-step blink permanents, ETB doublers, and activated/triggered flicker creatures. Wins via incremental value: every flicker re-fires Mulldrifter / Solemn Simulacrum / Sun Titan / Cloudblazer-style ETB triggers, often doubled by Panharmonicon-class effects.
_status_note: Live recipe — Gate 2 (canon) + Gate 3 (recipe) approved 2026-05-14 by local-board via comment 3ab6079e. 22/22 = 100% canon recall validated empirically against Scryfall API. Canon expanded 20→22 mid-review on board comment d2d5f66b to cover the TLA airbend mechanic (exile-and-recast-for-{2}) as a flicker variant.

canon_provenance.from_existing_decks: the-white-forge is the only deck currently tagged etb-flicker. From that deck the canon takes Teleportation Circle (recurring end-step flicker), Ephemerate (cheapest rebound flicker), Conjurer's Closet (recurring permanent flicker — added to canon for the etb-flicker prototype even though the live deck rotates it in/out), Panharmonicon (ETB doubler) and Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines (ETB doubler + opponent-ETB hoser). Solemn Simulacrum and Sun Titan are present in the deck but are pure ETB-value bodies that overlap with ramp/graveyard-reanimator recipes, so they sit outside canon and surface via those archetypes instead.
canon_provenance.from_edhrec_archetype_pages: EDHREC's flicker / blink landing pages anchor on Brago, Soulherder, Yorion, Felidar Guardian, Eldrazi Displacer, Restoration Angel, Reflector Mage, Mulldrifter as the canonical cards. From that set Soulherder is the cleanest activated end-step flicker creature; Cloudshift / Essence Flux / Momentary Blink / Acrobatic Maneuver are the staple cheap targeted flicker instants. Eerie Interlude and Ghostway are the canonical mass-flicker save-from-board-wipe spells. Wispweaver Angel + Distinguished Conjurer represent the ETB-flicker-yourself creatures. Far Traveler is the modern background commander pattern for recurring end-step flicker.
canon_provenance.from_combo_pieces: Commander Spellbook combo lines for flicker hinge on Felidar Guardian + Saheeli Rai (infinite Cat tokens) and Brago + Strionic Resonator (infinite ETBs); both lines route through the etb-doublers and flicker-activated-creatures sub-recipes. Emiel the Blessed + Pestermite / Deceiver Exarch is another archetype combo line, anchoring Emiel in canon. Gilraen, Dúnedain Protector is the LOTR-era activated flicker analog, included to test the recipe surfaces newer printings, not just MH-era staples.
canon_provenance.from_doubler_family: Yarok, the Desecrated, Naban, Dean of Iteration and Virtue of Knowledge are the conditional or alternate-cost variants of Panharmonicon — they all use the literal 'triggers an additional time' idiom, anchoring the etb_doublers sub-recipe to a deterministic Scryfall query rather than relying on partial-match phrases.
canon_provenance.from_airbend_variant: TLA (Avatar: The Last Airbender, 2025-11-21) introduced the airbend keyword: 'exile target permanent; while exiled, its owner may cast it for {2}'. Functionally this is flicker-with-a-mana-tax — every airbend recast re-fires ETBs and stacks with Panharmonicon-class doublers. The legacy sub-recipes (which all require the 'return ... to the battlefield' idiom) miss every airbend card, so the canon adds the two strongest payoffs and a dedicated airbend sub-recipe. Appa, Steadfast Guardian is the flash/flying ETB-airbender that creates Ally tokens whenever you cast from exile (the recast loop itself draws value). Aang, Airbending Master converts every creature leaving without dying into experience counters, then mints Ally tokens per counter on upkeep — the experience engine pairs natively with both airbend and the rest of the flicker package.

flicker_targeted_spells.intent: Cheap instants and sorceries that exile a single target creature you control and return it to the battlefield — the workhorse 'flicker spell' bucket. Used to re-fire ETBs at instant speed, dodge removal, untap a tapped attacker, or activate a doubler trigger.
queries: f:commander -t:creature -t:land o:"exile target" o:"return" o:"battlefield" o:"you control"

canon_recall.note: 24-result query, EDHREC-ordered. All 5 canon land in the top 15. Noise is bounded — every result is a flicker effect by construction; the only judgement calls are pirate/spirit/bird-tribal flavours (Splash Portal, Siren's Ruse) which still flicker a creature and re-fire its ETB, so they're tribe-flavoured variants of the same idiom, not false positives.

flicker_mass_spells.intent: Single-card mass blinks — exile every (or any number of) creature(s) you control and return them at end of turn. The classic save-from-Wrath answer that also re-fires the whole board's ETBs in one shot.
queries: f:commander -t:creature -t:land (o:"exile each creature you control" or o:"exile any number of target creatures you control")

canon_recall.note: 2-result query — every match is the canonical mass-flicker idiom. Zero noise. Semester's End is the closest cousin in the broader pool but uses 'exile each creature, planeswalker, and battle you control' phrasing — recipe accepts surfacing it only via the broader 'exile + return' family below if a deck needs it.

flicker_endstep_permanents.intent: Permanents (artifacts and enchantments) that re-fire flicker every end step — the recurring engine pieces that turn the deck from 'flicker package' into 'flicker engine'.
queries: f:commander -t:creature -t:land o:"at the beginning of your end step" o:"exile" o:"return"

canon_recall.note: 6-result query. The other 3 results — Airbender Ascension (TLA, quest-counter gated), Nahiri's Resolve (delayed return next upkeep, RW), Spirit-Sister's Call (graveyard reanimation that exiles-on-leave, BW) — are recipe-adjacent and worth surfacing to the board for case-by-case adoption. They're not false positives in the strict sense; they're flicker-via-end-step with extra friction.

etb_doublers.intent: Permanents that make every ETB trigger fire twice. The reason flicker is a deck and not just a removal-dodge. Doubles Mulldrifter draws, doubles Solemn Simulacrum ramps, doubles Sun Titan returns, doubles every flicker payoff.
queries: f:commander o:"entering causes a triggered ability" o:"triggers an additional time"

canon_recall.note: 6-result query (only Ancient Greenwarden is non-canon — it's the lands-entering variant, true positive for lands-matter overlap rather than noise). Zero noise inside the etb-doubler family. Strionic Resonator is NOT surfaced because it uses 'copy target triggered ability' phrasing — it is intentionally left out of this sub-recipe; it surfaces via spellbook combo discovery on a per-deck basis when Brago / Aminatou are the commander.

flicker_activated_creatures.intent: Creatures whose printed ability flickers another creature you control — either activated (Emiel, Gilraen, Distinguished Conjurer, Nephalia Smuggler) or triggered (Soulherder, Wispweaver Angel). The 'flicker on a body' bucket: every one of these stacks with the etb_doublers above for recurring value loops.
queries: f:commander t:creature o:"exile another target creature you control" o:"return"

canon_recall.note: 9-result query. Non-canon results — Lilysplash Mentor (+1/+1 counter variant, GU), Kykar Zephyr Awakener (spellslinger-conditional flicker, UW commander), Nephalia Smuggler (mono-U 1-mana repeatable), Baboon Spirit (Spirit-tribal flicker) — are all legitimate etb-flicker tools but were ranked below canon for adoption simplicity. Eldrazi Displacer is intentionally NOT in canon: its text reads 'exile another target creature' without the 'you control' qualifier (it can also exile opponent creatures as removal), and so falls outside this sub-recipe's scope. Decks running Displacer should treat it as cross-archetype with stax-control / removal.

airbend_flicker_variant.intent: TLA-era airbend cards: exile a permanent you control; while exiled, its owner may recast it for {2}. Functionally flicker-with-a-mana-tax — each recast re-fires ETBs and stacks with Panharmonicon-class doublers. Mono-white only today (every printed airbend card is W or contains W). Caller decks must budget {2} per re-fire and treat airbend as deliberate-flicker, not free-flicker.

canon_recall.note: 13-result query, all true positives — the keyword filter is deterministic. Other results worth surfacing to decks adopting airbend: Appa, Loyal Sky Bison (flying ETB+attack airbender, {4}{W}{W}), Aang, the Last Airbender ({3}{W} flying airbender with lesson-tribal lifelink), Monk Gyatso (reactive airbend on targeted-creature trigger), Airbender Ascension (quest-counter enchantment, conditional end-step flicker), Glider Staff (equipment airbender), Avatar's Wrath / Whirlwind Technique / Airbending Lesson / Airbender's Reversal (instants and sorceries). Zero noise — the keyword filter excludes any non-airbend card by construction.

noise_budget.policy: Each sub-recipe is anchored to a single oracle-text idiom or keyword and bounded by the f:commander filter; surfaced result counts range from 2 to 24, and false-positive rate across the recipe is <10% (every non-canon result is either a tribe-flavoured variant or a same-idiom new printing, not a different mechanic). The airbend_flicker_variant sub-recipe uses keyword:airbend which is zero-noise by construction.
noise_budget.color_identity_handling: All queries are deck-color-agnostic. At runtime the calling deck splices its commander color identity via id<=<colors> (e.g. id<=wu for Soulherder decks) onto each sub-recipe query. Mono-white decks (the-white-forge today) will not surface Soulherder / Yarok / Wispweaver / Emiel / Gilraen as adoption candidates — that's correct: those cards are illegal in mono-white. The full canon recall figures above are color-unfiltered.
noise_budget.airbend_mana_tax: Airbend recasts cost {2} per permanent. Caller decks adopting airbend should hold {2} open per intended re-fire, or pair with cost-reducers (e.g. Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn for Ally-tribal Appa decks). Unlike free-flicker (Cloudshift, Ephemerate) airbend cannot be infinite-comboed off zero-cost recasts — treat it as deliberate-flicker rather than combo-flicker.

cross_archetype_overlap.graveyard-reanimator: Sun Titan, Karmic Guide, and Reveillark are flicker-adjacent (recur creatures with ETBs from the graveyard) but live in the graveyard-reanimator recipe — etb-flicker should not duplicate them.
cross_archetype_overlap.artifacts-matter: Solemn Simulacrum, Mycosynth Wellspring, Ichor Wellspring, Junk Diver, Myr Retriever, Scrap Trawler are ETB-payoff artifacts that pair with flicker but anchor to artifacts-matter — etb-flicker assumes them as background.
cross_archetype_overlap.spellslinger: Brago + Strionic Resonator and Felidar Guardian + Saheeli Rai are flicker combo lines but surface via Commander Spellbook's find-my-combos pass on a per-deck basis, not via etb-flicker queries.
